title: "Presenter notes"
subtitle: "Running order, checkpoints, and the room-plus-Zoom plan."
---

## Before the day

- [ ] Confirm with the organizer how remote questions reach the room, and who monitors the Zoom chat. Do not plan to read the chat while presenting.
- [ ] The published description invites participants to "bring messy historical datasets". Open by saying the hour works on one finished dataset and that [Your own data](steps/07-your-data.qmd) is the take-home.
- [ ] Download `combined_mobility.mp4` from the col_matching site to the presenting laptop in case the room's network is slow; the opening slide streams it.
- [ ] Test the WikidataMCP endpoint from a non-campus network the day before. Rate limit is about five calls a second; the vector search takes one to two seconds a call.
- [ ] Decide which chatbot to use live for the control, or show the saved Gemini run. Either way have `outputs/ground-test/gemini-scoring.md` open.
- [ ] Print the [handout](handout.qmd) (one page, 25 copies).
- [ ] Rehearse against the clock with the saved checkpoints. Protect minutes 30–47.
- [ ] Put the site URL and both exercise URLs on the first slide. Someone posts them in the Zoom chat at the start.

## Slides

[slides.html](slides.html) is the deck, with speaker notes (press `S` in the browser). The first slide is the video as a full-screen background; let it run.

## Running order

| Min | Step | Live or saved | Checkpoint if behind |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–5 | [The atlas](steps/01-atlas.qmd) | The video, then the three numbers and the loop | Skip Trading Consequences |
| 5–12 | [The source](steps/02-source.qmd) | Entries on screen; participants mark one up (annotate page or paper) | Cut the mark-up to two minutes, Balmer only |
| 12–22 | [Structure](steps/03-structure.qmd) | Optional live: paste one entry into Claude Code with the prompt. Otherwise the saved Trimen record and the three audit examples | Audit numbers and the "not a bigger model" point |
| 22–30 | [Clean](steps/04-identity.qmd) | Saved: the four clusters | Abery/Carbery and A'Beckett only |
| 30–40 | [Ground](steps/05-ground.qmd) | Live: three MCP searches. Then the Gemini control (saved) | Saved lookups in `outputs/ground-test/answer-key.md` |
| 40–47 | [The map finds the errors](steps/06-loop.qmd) | Saved: Brewster, South Africa, Baluchistan, on the live atlas if the network allows | Brewster only |
| 47–55 | [Exercise](review/index.html) | R1–R6; show of hands and chat summaries on R2 and R6 | R1, R3, R6 |
| 55–60 | [Your own data](steps/07-your-data.qmd) and questions | | |

## The live lookup

Three searches, in this order, with the statements read aloud for the first two: Trimen (supported), Price (supported, and the gate had rejected it), Tibbits (nothing; record the search). If the endpoint is down, the same three are written up on the Ground page.

## The control

Jim's Gemini 3.8 Flash run of 7 October is scored in `outputs/ground-test/gemini-scoring.md`: zero of sixteen person identifiers, six not even people, seven near-miss numbers. Jim's Opus 5.5 run with web retrieval, same day, is scored in `outputs/ground-test/opus-scoring.md`: sixteen of sixteen, Prince found, the Gorges duplicate found, out of tool calls before any place. Show the three-column slide. If running a chatbot live, use entry 4 (Archer) or 18 (Marsh): both produced a near-miss number in Gemini, which makes the point better than a wild one.

## Online participation

- Remote participants see the same pages and both exercises. Nothing requires a login.
- Both exercise pages have a **Copy summary** button that produces one line for the Zoom chat, so the chat monitor can read decisions out.
- The decision exercise can **Download TSV** with reasons. If the organizers want them collected, say where to send the file.
- The atlas at jimclifford.ca/col_matching works in any browser; invite remote participants to search a name while the room marks up entries.

## What not to claim

- The audit numbers are from one 186-record sample of the structuring stage; they are not an accuracy rate for the whole graph.
- The silver standard measured the deterministic tier; the model judge's agreement rates were still pending in September.
- The published counts in the col_matching README, stats file and atlas disagreed in September; the numbers on these pages are from `kg_stats.json` and the atlas `meta.json` of 4 September 2026, copied into `outputs/atlas/`.
- The Gemini control is one run of one model with one prompt. It shows the failure mode; it does not rank models.
